messages:
maria: FYI CI publish for js-sdk failed on the typegen step after the semver bump. Publishing blocked.
ci-bot: [CI] job 5699 failed: https://ci.redwood/jobs/5699 — artifact: /artifacts/typegen-regendiff-5699.txt
alex: Repro locally. `yarn typegen:regen` produces files that only differ in property ordering in generated models. No semantic change but regen diff is non-empty.
priyanka: Did anything change in the changelog automation? I noticed some entries were moved around in the release script yesterday. Could that affect generator inputs?
sam: Also seeing sample-app e2e flake. Our mock server asserts header ordering for the auth/retry tests and the generated typings now change serialization order so snapshots fail intermittently.
tobias: Hm. Ordering-only diffs should be normalized. Where is the nondeterminism coming from — openapi generator, ts printer, or typegen wrapper?
ajex: (typo) 
alex: investigating — looks like the OpenAPI document got normalized differently because the changelog step runs a script that rewrites example objects (it adds keys in a deterministic order based on git tree traversal). The semver bump changed the git tree SHA ordering so traversal order changed. Weird but plausible.
jess: Can we add a stable sort in the typegen pipeline as a short-term fix? E.g., sort object keys before printing.
alex: Yup. Patch ready to sort keys in the generator output. Will open a tiny PR to normalize ordering and re-run CI.
priyanka: Small ask — add a test that runs `yarn typegen:regen` and asserts no diff against committed artifacts to catch this earlier in PRs.
sam: Agree. Also add a note in release checklist: run regen locally after changelog automation steps.
ci-bot: [CI] rerun requested by alex — job 5701 queued.
maria: Thanks team. If we can get a hotfix merge and a clean regen, we can unblock the publish tonight.
ci-bot: [CI] job 5701 passed: https://ci.redwood/jobs/5701 — no diff found. Publish unblocked. :tada:
